tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: List configured ESPHome devices with their online state, address and deployed firmware version. Scalar fields only; per-device lists such as loaded integrations come from get_config_components.

tools.name: get_config
tools.description: Read a device's YAML configuration, or secrets.yaml (its values then enter this conversation).

tools.name: update_config
tools.description: Replace a device's YAML configuration with new content. Read it with get_config first, pass that text as expected, and change only what is needed; run validate_config or compile afterwards. Add or change an automation with upsert_automation instead. The previous text stays in the dashboard's version history.

expected.description: The text get_config returned, verbatim; the write is refused with precondition_failed if the file changed since, so nothing is overwritten unseen.

tools.name: add_component
tools.description: Add a catalog component to a device config and save it. Use search_components to find the id and get_component for its fields.

fields.description: Config values keyed by field name; nested blocks are nested objects.

tools.name: validate_config
tools.description: Validate a device config with esphome and return the last output lines (truncated says whether earlier lines were dropped; esphome's concealed values show as <removed>).

tail_lines.description: Output lines to keep from the end.

tools.name: compile
tools.description: Queue a firmware compile for a device. Returns a job id to poll with get_job.

tools.name: install
tools.description: Compile and install firmware on a device. Returns the compile job id and the dependent upload job id; poll both with get_job. An offline device gets the update queued for its next wake (deferred, upload_job_id null). A flash has no undo: the device runs whatever compiles, so read and validate the config first.

port.description: 'OTA' (default), a serial port, or an IP/hostname.

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Get a firmware job's status, progress, exit code and the last output lines.

job_id.description: Firmware job id returned by compile or install.

tail_lines.description: Output lines to keep from the end.

tools.name: cancel_job
tools.description: Cancel a queued or running firmware job. Returns the job's status right after the request: a queued job is cancelled at once, a running one is signalled and may still finish, so poll get_job for its final status. A null status means the job already left the retained history.

job_id.description: Firmware job id returned by compile or install.

tools.name: search_components
tools.description: Search the ESPHome component catalog by name or keyword. total above the number of rows returned means the query was capped; narrow it.

tools.name: get_component
tools.description: Get a component's documentation: description, docs URL and every config field with type, description, required flag and allowed values. default_value is what ESPHome uses when the key is absent; an omitted flag is false. Advanced and YAML-only fields are omitted unless include_advanced is true.

platform.description: Target platform (esp32, esp8266, ...) to resolve platform defaults.

board_id.description: Board id from search_boards; resolves the chip variant's defaults, which platform alone cannot.

tools.name: get_config_components
tools.description: List the catalog components a device config used as of its last scan (every save rescans), with a short description and docs URL for each. Call get_component for the fields of any of them.

tools.name: search_boards
tools.description: Search the board catalog by name or chip; returns board ids for create_device. total above the number of rows returned means the query was capped; narrow it.

tools.name: list_secret_names
tools.description: List the secret names defined in secrets.yaml. Reference one in YAML as '!secret <name>'.

tools.name: set_secret
tools.description: Create one secret in secrets.yaml, the only way to change that file, or replace one with overwrite. Replacing is not recoverable: secrets.yaml is kept out of version history. Reference the secret in YAML as '!secret <name>'.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing value; the old one is lost.

tools.name: create_device
tools.description: Create a new device YAML with the wizard. Wi-Fi is written as '!secret wifi_ssid' and '!secret wifi_password' (set them first with set_secret if list_secret_names lacks them); it takes no Wi-Fi arguments. Returns the new configuration filename.

tools.name: list_automations
tools.description: List the automations a device config contains (scripts, intervals, api actions, on_* triggers, light effects) with their YAML, line range and location. Add or change one with upsert_automation; remove one with delete_automation.

tools.name: get_available_automations
tools.description: The triggers, actions, conditions, scripts and component instances this device's config makes available for automations, by id. Call this before upsert_automation: ESPHome has no automation block; a trigger is an on_* key under esphome (device level) or under the component entry it belongs to, and scripts and intervals are top-level script and interval lists. An omitted list is empty.

tools.name: get_automation_docs
tools.description: Documentation for automation building blocks: the fields each trigger, action, condition, light effect or filter takes. An omitted flag is false; advanced and YAML-only fields are omitted unless include_advanced is true.

tools.name: upsert_automation
tools.description: Insert or replace one automation in a device config and save it; the backend renders the YAML in the right place, so never splice YAML by hand. An insert must not replace existing YAML; to replace, pass the automation's raw_yaml from list_automations as expected. The tool checks the shape, not the fields: esphome does that, and the reply's validation is the validate_config result for the saved file; when validation is null the run did not finish inside the call budget, so run validate_config. Repair what esphome reports by replacing the automation, with expected from a fresh list_automations.

component_id.description: component_on, component_action, light_effect: the component instance id, devices[].id from get_available_automations (not the catalog type in devices[].component_id).

trigger.description: device_on, component_on: the bare on_* YAML key, e.g. 'on_press'.

index.description: interval, light_effect: list position; the current list length appends. device_on, component_on: only for a list-shaped handler, from list_automations.

field.description: component_action: the action-list field as a dot path from the instance, e.g. 'turn_on_action' or 'valves.0.set_action'.

location.description: Where the automation lives: a location from list_automations, or a new one whose keys follow its kind.

trigger_params.description: The block's own keys: a trigger's fields; interval's interval period; script's mode and parameters; api_action's variables; for light_effect exactly one key, the effect id mapped to its params; nothing for component_action.

actions.description: The actions to run, in order.

action_id.description: Action id from get_available_automations, e.g. 'light.turn_on'; an uncatalogued action needs unknown.

children.description: Control flow branches: a branch name such as 'then' or 'else' mapped to a list of actions shaped like this item.

conditions.description: The boolean gate of an if, while or wait_until.

children.description: A combinator's sub-conditions, each shaped like this item.

branches.description: A choose action's ordered choices, each {conditions: [...], actions: [...]}; its default list is children.else.

unknown.description: True for an uncatalogued action, such as an external component's: raw_body is written verbatim and params, children and conditions are not used.

raw_body.description: The uncatalogued action's YAML body, verbatim.

automation.description: The automation tree; the location decides the trigger, so no trigger_id.

expected.description: When replacing: the automation's raw_yaml exactly as list_automations returned it.

tools.name: delete_automation
tools.description: Remove one automation from a device config and save it; pass the location and raw_yaml from list_automations. A location is positional, so the delete is refused with precondition_failed if the automation changed or moved since it was listed. The reply's validation is as on upsert_automation.

component_id.description: component_on, component_action, light_effect: the component instance id, devices[].id from get_available_automations (not the catalog type in devices[].component_id).

trigger.description: device_on, component_on: the bare on_* YAML key, e.g. 'on_press'.

index.description: interval, light_effect: list position; the current list length appends. device_on, component_on: only for a list-shaped handler, from list_automations.

field.description: component_action: the action-list field as a dot path from the instance, e.g. 'turn_on_action' or 'valves.0.set_action'.

location.description: The automation's location as returned by list_automations.

expected.description: The automation's raw_yaml exactly as list_automations returned it.
